title: Kernel + KV Cache + Batching Sync — action plan and runbook
body:
Attendees: Avery Chen (owner), Diego Marquez, Priya Patel, Samira Iqbal, Jon Park

Summary (high level):
This sync focused on concretizing next-week experiments and an initial canary rollout plan for the combined kernel refactor + KV cache eviction change + adaptive batching behavior. We reviewed microbenchmarks performed on g4dn-like nodes and a small Dedicated pool (4x A10g equiv). Early results show a consistent P50 improvement for short sequences (<64 tokens) when using the new fused-attention kernel, but a small P99 regression for long-context workloads (>1024) under heavy concurrency. The KV cache change (LRU + time-decay flag) cuts repeated-prefix work by ~22% in synthetic prefix-heavy traces. Batching heuristics reduced per-token overhead for throughput workloads but introduced 5–10ms tail jitter in low-traffic islands.

Decisions made this sync:
- Kernel: proceed with the fused-attention kernel for default short-sequence path. Flag-controlled fallback to legacy kernel for long-context/high-concurrency requests. Reason: measurable P50 win and code complexity acceptable when fallback is gated.
- KV cache eviction: adopt hybrid LRU + time-decay (TTL) policy behind a feature flag. TTL default 15m for interactive sessions, 60s for ephemeral streamed requests. This balances memory growth vs. cache hit stability on sticky sessions.
- Batching: enable adaptive batching on Dedicated by default for route "text.generate" with conservative patience (10ms) and max batch 64. For hosted API, keep current conservative config and run a 2-week canary on the EU region.

Microbenchmark summary (source: local perf harness, test cluster perf-qa-03):
- Test matrix: seq_len in {16, 64, 256, 1024}, concurrency in {8, 32, 128}, batch cap {8,32,64}
- Fused-attn kernel: seq16 P50 -25% latency vs baseline, seq64 P50 -18%, seq1024 P99 +12% at concurrency 128
- KV cache (LRU vs hybrid): synthetic prefix trace hit-rate improved from 44% to 54%; p99 tokens saved per request increased for streaming workloads
- Batching tweaks: patience 5ms -> 10ms lowered P99 token cost by 6% for throughput tests, but introduced up to 9ms added latency in cold-start single-client traces

Key risks / open questions:
- NUMA pinning and memory fragmentation: Samira observed increased malloc stalls during long-context tests when the fused kernel runs alongside the new KV allocator. Root cause unclear — could be allocator+kernel memory access pattern.
- P99 regression for long-context under heavy concurrency: need deeper profiling (sampling + perf counters) to determine whether it's kernel compute-bound or IO/serialization overhead.
- Cache eviction tuning: TTL 15m default is conservative but might cause memory pressure on Dedicated pockets with large numbers of long-lived sessions. We need an eviction monitor and auto-throttle policy.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Diego: run perf counters (L1/L2 misses, DRAM bandwidth) on seq1024 concurrency 128 case, attach perf reports to PR-457. ETA: 2026-03-13.
- Priya: instrument KV cache with a lightweight eviction telemetry endpoint (per-route cache size, hits, evictions) and push to the console metrics pipeline. ETA: 2026-03-16.
- Samira: reproduce the malloc stalls locally with ASAN+jemalloc stats, try alternate allocator flags (background_decommit, per arena pin). Report by 2026-03-15.
- Jon: prepare canary plan doc for EU Hosted + Dedicated pilot; include rollback criteria and SLO checkpoints. Draft by 2026-03-12.
- Avery: coordinate a 30-minute deep-dive on Wednesday to review Diego's perf counters and Samira's allocator findings. Meeting invite sent; aim 2026-03-11 10:00 PT.

Canary / rollout plan (short):
1) Merge kernel and KV cache feature flags behind config defaults (PRs 457, 462).
2) Deploy to perf-qa nodes, run smoke harness for 24h (verify p50/p99 within guardrails).
3) Canary to EU hosted endpoints for 48h with 10% traffic split; monitor token-level latency, cache hit-rate, memory RSS per process.
4) If no regressions >10% p99 or unexplained OOMs, expand to Dedicated pilot (two Reserved pools) for 72h.
5) Gradual global rollout with rollback automated on SLO triggers.

Testing and verification checklist:
- Unit tests for new kernel ops (coverage target 95%).
- Integration test: end-to-end KV cache warmup using historical prefix traces.
- Load test: synthetic concurrency matrix with golden trace comparing token throughput and latency deltas.
- Memory safety: run long-run (24h) perf test under high-concurrency to catch fragmentation.

Notes and context (fragments saved from discussion):
- Diego: "I think the fallback path must be zero-copy to avoid undoing the p50 improvements."
- Priya: "We should expose a console heatmap showing per-route cache amplification; will help product set realistic TTLs."
- Samira: "Allocator interactions are the usual suspect; try isolating fused kernel on its own NUMA node as a diagnostic."

Related links/references:
- PR 457: fused-attention kernel implementation (see bench harness in tests/perf).
- PR 462: KV cache TTL + eviction policy.
- JIRA-RWD-3124: long-context p99 regression investigation ticket.
- Slack thread: serving-runtime #kernel-kv-batching (link above).

Stretch goals for next sprint:
- Explore per-request cache affinity tokens (client-scoped cache keys) to reduce cross-client pollution.
- Evaluate kernel autotuner that selects kernel based on seq_len histogram over a 5-minute window.

Meeting artifacts to attach before merge: Diego's perf tarball, Priya's metrics schema PR, Samira's allocator repro script. Place attachments in the PR description and reference in the canary doc.

If you were at the meeting: review your assigned action item and update the doc with progress notes. If you couldn't attend, please read Diego's perf notes and drop a comment in the PR that you reviewed the metrics.

End of notes.
